name: Hydrochlorothiazide and skin cancer risk
summary: Pharmacoepidemiologic studies underpinning the IARC evaluation link hydrochlorothiazide use to an increased risk of keratinocyte carcinoma, with a strong dose-response for squamous-cell carcinoma and a smaller association with basal-cell carcinoma.
description: The 2025 IARC Monograph summary (Cogliano et al., Lancet Oncology) classifies hydrochlorothiazide largely on the basis of pharmacoepidemiologic studies of photocarcinogenesis. This topic assembles the principal underlying studies: nationwide/population-based case-control studies from Denmark (Pedersen 2018) and Iceland (Adalsteinsson 2021) and a large US cohort in the FDA Sentinel system (Eworuke 2021).
interpretation: The association is strongest and dose-dependent for squamous-cell carcinoma, particularly in the high-cumulative-dose Danish data; basal-cell carcinoma associations are small. The US cohort (comparing HCTZ with ACE inhibitors) found only modest excess risk overall, concentrated among lighter-skinned users. Exposure contrasts differ across studies (high cumulative dose vs any use) and none could adjust for sun exposure or skin type, so between-study heterogeneity is expected and confounding cannot be excluded.
methodologyNotes: Each study's principal reported adjusted effect and 95% CI are copied verbatim; the exposure contrast is stated per study. Odds ratios (case-control) and hazard ratios (cohort) are entered as reported and treated by the engine as risk-ratio approximations (flagged). No baseline risk is entered (sources report incident rates or matched-set odds, not a directly transferable control risk), so absolute-risk translation is not shown.

studies.author: Pedersen
studies.citation: Pedersen SA, Gaist D, Schmidt SAJ, Hölmich LR, Friis S, Pottegård A. Hydrochlorothiazide use and risk of nonmelanoma skin cancer: A nationwide case-control study from Denmark. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2018;78(4):673-681.e9.
studies.population: Danish Cancer Registry NMSC cases 2004–2012, matched 1:20 by age and sex
studies.endpointDefinition: SCC associated with high cumulative HCTZ use (≥50,000 mg).
studies.notes: High-use estimate (≥50,000 mg); clear dose-response (≥200,000 mg OR 7.38, 95% CI 6.32–8.60).

studies.author: Adalsteinsson
studies.citation: Adalsteinsson JA, Muzumdar S, Waldman R, et al. Association between hydrochlorothiazide and the risk of in situ and invasive squamous cell skin carcinoma and basal cell carcinoma: A population-based case-control study. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2021;84(3):669-675.
studies.endpointDefinition: Invasive SCC associated with cumulative HCTZ dose above 37,500 mg.
studies.notes: Invasive SCC, high cumulative dose (>37,500 mg). SCC in situ OR 1.24 (1.01–1.52).

studies.author: Eworuke
studies.citation: Eworuke E, Haug N, Bradley M, et al. Risk of Nonmelanoma Skin Cancer in Association With Use of Hydrochlorothiazide-Containing Products in the United States. JNCI Cancer Spectr. 2021;5(2):pkab009.
studies.population: US FDA Sentinel System, 5.2 million propensity-matched HCTZ vs ACE-inhibitor users
studies.endpointDefinition: SCC in HCTZ vs ACE-inhibitor users, overall population.
studies.notes: Comparator is ACE inhibitors (not non-use). Overall estimate; risk higher among Caucasians (HR 1.15, 1.12–1.17).
